speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when these symptoms of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and arm weakness first started, and have they been getting progressively worse? Also, do you notice any changes in your vision or strength depending on the time of day or after you've been active?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing, choking on food or liquids, or changes in your facial expressions and speech? I would also like to know if you have had any recent respiratory infections or if your symptoms fluctuate more noticeably in the evenings.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR Antibody Test. Given your fluctuating weakness and double vision that worsens with activity, I need to check for antibodies associated with Myasthenia Gravis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated). Additional findings supporting the diagnosis include ptosis worsening with sustained upward gaze, diminished motor strength in upper extremities, and electromyography showing decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation. Chest CT is normal with no thymoma detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results confirm the presence of acetylcholine receptor antibodies, and combined with your fluctuating weakness and eye symptoms, the picture is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.
